MUQATIL:9:118/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:118/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:118/r1.claim: The three left behind were Murara b. Rabi'a, Hilal b. Umayya, and Ka'b b. Malik; unlike Abu Lubaba and his companions, they had not acted as he did.

MUQATIL:9:118/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:118/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:118/r2.claim: For a month, people would not speak to, visit, trade with, or buy from the three, and even their families stopped speaking to them.

MUQATIL:9:118/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:9:118/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:9:118/r3.claim: The earth felt constricted because no one mixed with them; they became certain there was no refuge from God except in him, so he accepted their repentance.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p290#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p290#3/r1.speaker: عكرمة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p290#3/r1.claim: Ikrima explains that the three who were left behind were held back from repentance.

AKHFASH:v1p368/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v1p368/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v1p368/r1.claim: At a pause, ملجأ has no final alif because it has no tanwīn; by contrast, a pause on the tanwīn accusative ملجأً retains alif.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p193#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p193#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p193#4/r1.claim: The earth felt tight around them despite its spaciousness.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p193#4/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p193#4/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p193#4/r2.claim: They became certain that nothing would save them from God and His punishment except God Himself.

TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r1.claim: The three are the people deferred for God’s decision in 9:106; God later accepted their repentance. “Held back” means their repentance was deferred while others were forgiven.

TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r2.claim: Ikrima explains that the three were held back from receiving repentance.

TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r3.claim: Qatada likewise says the three were held back from repentance.

TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r4.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r4.claim: The earth felt narrow despite its breadth because they grieved and regretted missing the campaign with the Messenger; their own selves felt constricted by distress.

TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r5.claim: They became certain that no refuge from God’s trial or feared punishment existed except with God; He then granted them a return to obedience so they could comply with His commands and prohibitions.

TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r6.claim: God is the one who grants and enables repentance to whomever He wills, and is merciful not to punish after repentance or abandon a servant seeking to repent.

TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r7.speaker: جابر
TAB-FULL:v12p53#2/r7.claim: Jabir identifies the three as Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn Rabi'a, all from the Ansar.

TAB-FULL:v12p56/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r1.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r1.claim: Ikrima says the three were deferred in the middle of Surat Bara'a.

TAB-FULL:v12p56/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r2.claim: Mujahid says the three deferred in the middle of Bara'a were Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara ibn Rabi'a, and Ka'b ibn Malik.

TAB-FULL:v12p56/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r3.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r3.claim: Mujahid also identifies them as the deferred group and names all three as Ansar.

TAB-FULL:v12p56/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r4.speaker: سعيد
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r4.claim: Sa'id names Ka'b ibn Malik, the poet, Murara ibn al-Rabi', and Hilal ibn Umayya as the three, all Ansar.

TAB-FULL:v12p56/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r5.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r5.claim: Al-Dahhak likewise identifies all three as Ansar: Hilal, Murara, and Ka'b.

TAB-FULL:v12p56/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v12p56/r6.claim: Qatada names Ka'b, Hilal, and Murara as the three who missed the Tabuk expedition; he recounts their remorse and different acts while awaiting the Prophet’s response.

TAB-FULL:v12p57/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says God accepted repentance from the Prophet, the Emigrants, the Helpers, and the three men.

TAB-FULL:v12p57/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r2.speaker: أبو مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r2.claim: Abu Malik identifies the three left behind as Hilal ibn Umayya, Kaʿb ibn Malik, and Murara ibn Rabiʿa.

TAB-FULL:v12p57/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r3.claim: ʿIkrima likewise names Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara, and Kaʿb as the three men.

TAB-FULL:v12p57/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r4.claim: Kaʿb recalls being unusually well supplied for the campaign but delaying preparation until the army had departed, after which the Prophet ordered people not to speak to them.

TAB-FULL:v12p57/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r5.speaker: ابن شهاب
TAB-FULL:v12p57/r5.claim: Ibn Shihab recounts Tabuk, the three named men and roughly eighty others staying behind; the three admitted fault truthfully, while others swore excuses and were accepted outwardly.

TAB-FULL:v12p59/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r1.claim: Kaʿb says he missed no expedition except Tabuk and Badr; no one was blamed for missing Badr because the Muslims had unexpectedly met their enemy while seeking a Quraysh caravan.

TAB-FULL:v12p59/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r2.claim: Kaʿb prized his pledge at al-ʿAqaba above even the better-known battle of Badr.

TAB-FULL:v12p59/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r3.claim: Kaʿb says the Prophet clarified the campaign's destination so Muslims could prepare; Kaʿb nevertheless delayed despite being unusually well supplied.

TAB-FULL:v12p59/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r4.claim: Kaʿb repeatedly failed to finish preparing, then regretted not catching up; after the army left, he saw no comparable stay-behind except a suspected hypocrite or an excused weak person.

TAB-FULL:v12p59/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r5.claim: At Tabuk the Prophet asked about Kaʿb; a man blamed his fine clothes, and the Prophet later recognized Abu Khaythama approaching through the mirage.

TAB-FULL:v12p59/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r6.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p59/r6.claim: When the Prophet was returning, Kaʿb considered inventing an excuse but resolved that no lie would save him and chose to tell the truth.

TAB-FULL:v12p61/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r1.claim: More than eighty stay-behinds offered excuses and oaths; the Prophet accepted their outward claims and left their inner states to God, but told Kaʿb that his truthful admission meant he must await God's judgment.

TAB-FULL:v12p61/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r2.claim: Kaʿb admitted having no excuse and hoped for God's forgiveness; the Prophet affirmed that he had told the truth and ordered him to wait for God's decision.

TAB-FULL:v12p61/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r3.claim: Men of Banu Salima urged Kaʿb to use the excuses others gave, and he nearly retracted, but learned that two others had made the same truthful admission.

TAB-FULL:v12p61/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p61/r4.claim: Kaʿb asks who else told the truth and is told two men made the same admission; Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ is first named.

TAB-FULL:v12p62/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r1.claim: Unlike the other absentees, the three were barred from conversation for fifty nights; people shunned them, while Kaʿb's two companions stayed home weeping and Kaʿb kept attending prayer and markets without being answered.

TAB-FULL:v12p62/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r2.claim: Kaʿb's cousin Abu Qatada would not answer whether Kaʿb loved God and His Messenger, finally saying that God and His Messenger knew best.

TAB-FULL:v12p62/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r3.claim: A man from Ghassan sent Kaʿb a letter inviting him to join the king because the Prophet had shunned him; Kaʿb treated the offer as another trial and burned it.

TAB-FULL:v12p62/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r4.claim: After forty nights the Prophet ordered the three to separate from their wives; Hilal's wife was allowed to serve him without intimacy, and Kaʿb sent his wife to her family.

TAB-FULL:v12p62/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p62/r5.claim: Kaʿb refused to ask permission for his wife to remain with him and completed fifty nights under the ban; at dawn he heard a caller announce good news.

TAB-FULL:v12p64/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r1.claim: On the fiftieth morning Kaʿb learned that God had accepted their repentance; people brought him the news, and the Prophet greeted him joyfully as having reached his best day.

TAB-FULL:v12p64/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r2.claim: Kaʿb offered to give all his property in charity, but the Prophet advised him to keep some; he retained his share at Khaybar.

TAB-FULL:v12p64/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r3.claim: Kaʿb vowed to speak only truth; he called honesty his greatest blessing and contrasted the truthful trio with the hypocrites condemned in the passage about false oaths.

TAB-FULL:v12p64/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p64/r4.claim: Kaʿb explains that the three were left in suspense by the Prophet's deferral of their judgment, unlike others whose sworn excuses were accepted; the phrase is not about simply missing the campaign.

TAB-FULL:v12p66/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v12p66/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
TAB-FULL:v12p66/r1.claim: A further transmission through Kaʿb's son repeats his account of the Tabuk absence; another report from Kaʿb notes that he missed only Tabuk and Badr, for which no one was reproached.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r1.claim: Ka'b says he was prosperous and able to travel, but repeatedly delayed preparing for Tabuk during the ripe harvest until the army had departed.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r2.claim: At Tabuk the Prophet asked about Ka'b; Muadh rejected a companion's claim that vanity had held him back and vouched that they knew only good of him.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r3.claim: Ka'b resolved to tell the truth rather than make up an excuse; the Prophet confirmed that he had spoken truthfully and deferred judgment to God.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r4.claim: Ka'b identifies the other two as Murara ibn al-Rabi and Hilal ibn Umayya, upright men who had witnessed Badr.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899#2/r5.claim: The Prophet ordered people not to speak to the three; during the fifty-night isolation, Ka'b alone kept attending prayer and the marketplace while all ignored him.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1899/r1.claim: Ka'b says he missed no campaign with the Prophet except Tabuk and Badr; no one was reproached for missing Badr because the Prophet had set out for the Quraysh caravan before unexpectedly meeting the enemy.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r1.claim: Ka'b's cousin Abu Qatada would not answer whether he loved God and the Prophet, except to say that God and His Messenger knew best; Ka'b wept and left.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r2.claim: A Syrian trader delivered the Ghassan king's offer of refuge after hearing Ka'b was shunned; Ka'b treated the offer as another trial and burned the letter.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r3.claim: On the fortieth night, the Prophet ordered Ka'b to stay apart from his wife without divorcing her; Ka'b sent her to her family.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1901/r4.claim: The Prophet allowed Hilal's elderly wife to serve him but prohibited marital relations; Ka'b refused his family's suggestion to seek the same exception.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r1.claim: After fifty nights, a caller announced God's acceptance of their repentance; Ka'b prostrated, and people hurried to congratulate him.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r2.claim: Ka'b gave his only clothes to the messenger who brought the news, borrowed replacements, and went to the Prophet as people congratulated him.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r3.claim: The Prophet called this the best day of Ka'b's life, and Ka'b asked whether the good news came from God.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r4.claim: When Ka'b vowed to give all his wealth in charity, the Prophet told him to keep his share at Khaybar.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1902/r5.claim: Ka'b connects his deliverance to truthfulness and vows to speak only truth; he says he has not knowingly lied since his confession.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r1.claim: Ka'b says no blessing after Islam felt greater than telling the Prophet the truth, since lying would have destroyed him as it destroyed the hypocrites.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r2.claim: Ka'b contrasts the three men's deferred judgment with the other absentees, whose excuses were accepted; he says the verse means their case was held back, not that they lagged behind the army.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1903/r3.claim: Hasan's report describes one of the three regretting that he stayed with his ripe orchard instead of joining the jihad and dedicating the orchard to God's cause.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r1.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r1.claim: In Hasan's account, another man regrets staying with his family and vows not to return to them or his property until God decides their case.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r2.claim: The third man vows either to die or catch up with the expedition; God then reveals the three men's repentance.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r3.speaker: الحسن
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r3.claim: Hasan marvels that they shed no blood, took no illicit wealth, and did not spread corruption, yet suffered greatly for merely delaying the campaign.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r4.claim: Qatada says the three were held back from repentance; they were Ka'b, Hilal, and Murara, and though they committed no other offense, they had stayed behind at Tabuk.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r5.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r5.claim: Qatada recounts that one tied himself to a pillar until released by the Prophet, another gave away his orchard, and the third walked through deserts to catch up, bleeding.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r6.speaker: الضحاك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1904/r6.claim: Al-Dahhak says they were left awaiting repentance until God accepted the repentance of Abu Lubaba and his companions; Abu Malik is also reported to say they were left from repentance.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r1.speaker: عكرمة بن خالد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r1.claim: Ikrima ibn Khalid reads خلفوا in the accusative, understanding the three as those who came after Muhammad and his Companions.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r2.claim: Ka'b recounts that while the earth and his soul felt constricted, he heard a caller on Mount Sal announcing good news and fell in prostration.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r3.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r3.claim: Mujahid says every use of ظن in the Quran denotes certainty.

IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v6p1905/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas says God initiated repentance so the three could repent, provided they remained steadfast; al-Dahhak is reported to agree.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r1.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r1.speaker: author
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r1.claim: The present form يستغفر narrates an anticipated event as though occurring now, a common Arabic device also used for past and future scenes.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r2.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r2.speaker: عكرمة وزر بن حبيش وعمرو بن عبيد
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r2.claim: The standard reading passivizes خُلّفوا, while these readers use خَلَفوا to mean they stayed behind; a further group reads خالفوا, meaning they opposed and thus remained behind.

IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r3.author: Ibn Jinnī
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر وعلي بن الحسين وجعفر بن محمد وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
IBNJINNI-MUHTASAB:v1p305/r3.claim: This group reads خالفوا; the author says its sense converges with 'stayed behind,' since their opposition resulted in remaining there.

SULAMI:v1p291#2/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p291#2/r1.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p291#2/r1.claim: Early signs of sincere repentance include feeling the earth and one's own condition constrict, fearing divine punishment at every breath, and finding refuge only in God after severing reliance on every means.

SULAMI:v1p291#2/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p291#2/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p291#2/r2.claim: The penitents relied on no beloved or intimate; their hearts were severed from all creatures and existents, since true knowledge requires attention to the Real alone.

SULAMI:v1p291#2/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p291#2/r3.speaker: الجنيد
SULAMI:v1p291#2/r3.claim: No one is saved except through truthful refuge in God.

SULAMI:v1p291#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p291#3/r1.speaker: أبو يزيد
SULAMI:v1p291#3/r1.claim: Asked for the root of sincere repentance, Abu Yazid answered that it comes through God and His enabling.

SULAMI:v1p291#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p291#3/r2.speaker: بعضهم
SULAMI:v1p291#3/r2.claim: God drew the penitents back through prior tenderness, grace, and kindness; He brought them to Himself rather than their returning by their own power.

SULAMI:v1p291#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p291#3/r3.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p291#3/r3.claim: God's compassionate turning toward creatures precedes the servant's obedience and return.

THALABI:v5p104#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p104#2/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p104#2/r6.claim: The three left behind were those who failed to join Tabuk; another view says their judgment was deferred after Abu Lubaba and his companions’ repentance.

THALABI:v5p104#2/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p104#2/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p104#2/r7.claim: The phrase about hearts almost turning is explained as near deviation because of the severe trial; readers differ between tāʾ and yāʾ, with al-Aʿmash intending a delayed subject.

THALABI:v5p105/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r1.speaker: عكرمة وحميد
THALABI:v5p105/r1.claim: They read khullifu with fatḥa and light consonants, meaning that the three came after the Prophet; Jaʿfar al-Sadiq reads khalafu and al-Aʿmash reads al-mukhallafin.

THALABI:v5p105/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v5p105/r2.claim: The three left behind were Kaʿb ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayya, all from the Ansar.

THALABI:v5p105/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p105/r3.claim: Kaʿb says he never missed a campaign except Badr and Tabuk; the Prophet did not censure Badr absentees because the expedition sought a caravan and the battle happened unexpectedly.

THALABI:v5p105/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p105/r4.claim: Kaʿb says he valued the pledge of al-ʿAqaba more than having been present at Badr.

THALABI:v5p105/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p105/r5.claim: Kaʿb says the Prophet usually concealed his military destination, but for Tabuk he wanted people to prepare openly because of the distance and hardship.

THALABI:v5p105/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r6.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p105/r6.claim: Though well equipped with two mounts and inclined to campaign, Kaʿb delayed during the pleasant shade and ripe fruit until the army had left.

THALABI:v5p105/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r7.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p105/r7.claim: In the city Kaʿb saw no other absentees except people suspected of hypocrisy or those excused for weakness; roughly eighty others had stayed behind.

THALABI:v5p105/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p105/r8.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p105/r8.claim: The Prophet did not ask about Kaʿb until reaching Tabuk, where he asked what had happened to him.

THALABI:v5p106#2/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106#2/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p106#2/r1.claim: Kaʿb’s relatives urged him to offer an excuse like the others, but after learning Hilal ibn Umayya and Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ also told the truth, he refused to lie.

THALABI:v5p106#2/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106#2/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p106#2/r2.claim: The Prophet ordered people not to speak to the three truthful absentees, beginning a prolonged social boycott.

THALABI:v5p106#2/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106#2/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p106#2/r3.claim: Kaʿb says the people and even familiar walls and land seemed changed; he went to the market and mosque, but the Prophet would not meet his gaze.

THALABI:v5p106#2/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106#2/r4.speaker: أبو قتادة
THALABI:v5p106#2/r4.claim: Abu Qatada would not confirm Kaʿb’s love for God and His Messenger, replying that God and His Messenger know best.

THALABI:v5p106#2/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106#2/r5.speaker: ملك غسان
THALABI:v5p106#2/r5.claim: The king of Ghassan invited Kaʿb to leave the Prophet’s community for a place where he would be supported; Kaʿb burned the letter as a trial.

THALABI:v5p106#2/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106#2/r6.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p106#2/r6.claim: The Prophet told Kaʿb to avoid his wife without divorcing her; he gave the same order regarding the wives of the other two, while allowing Hilal’s wife to serve him without intimacy.

THALABI:v5p106/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106/r1.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
THALABI:v5p106/r1.claim: When someone alleged that Kaʿb was vainly admiring his clothes and body, Muʿadh defended him, saying they knew nothing but good of him.

THALABI:v5p106/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p106/r2.claim: Seeing a man approach through the mirage, the Prophet recognized him as Abu Khaythama, who had given a measure of dates and been mocked by hypocrites.

THALABI:v5p106/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p106/r3.claim: On the return to Medina, Kaʿb weighed whether to escape the Prophet’s anger with a pretext, then chose truth as the only way to be saved.

THALABI:v5p106/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
THALABI:v5p106/r4.claim: Kaʿb admits he had no excuse and had never been more able or better equipped than when he stayed behind.

THALABI:v5p106/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p106/r5.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v5p106/r5.claim: The Prophet accepts Kaʿb’s confession as truthful and leaves his case to God’s judgment.

THALABI:v5p107/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p107/r1.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p107/r1.claim: Kaʿb’s wife said he remained motionless, bent over, and crying day and night after the affair.

THALABI:v5p107/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p107/r2.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p107/r2.claim: After fifty nights of the boycott, Kaʿb prayed at dawn on his roof, heard a herald from Mount Salʿ announce relief, and fell prostrate.

THALABI:v5p107/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p107/r3.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p107/r3.claim: The herald’s voice reached Kaʿb before the mounted messenger; Kaʿb gave him his clothes and borrowed garments to wear.

THALABI:v5p107/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p107/r4.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p107/r4.claim: The repentance revelation came late at night; Umm Salama urged the Prophet to announce it, and Talha alone among the Emigrants hurried to greet Kaʿb.

THALABI:v5p107/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p107/r5.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p107/r5.claim: Kaʿb asked whether his acceptance came from God or the Prophet; the Prophet answered that it came from God and recited the passage about God turning to the Prophet and Emigrants.

THALABI:v5p107/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p107/r6.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p107/r6.claim: Kaʿb vowed to give all his wealth in charity as repentance, but the Prophet advised him to keep some, so he retained his share from Khaybar.

THALABI:v5p107/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p107/r7.speaker: كعب
THALABI:v5p107/r7.claim: Kaʿb considered God’s blessing of truthful testimony greater than any post-Islam blessing and hoped to remain truthful; he says he had not lied since.

THALABI:v5p108/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p108/r1.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v5p108/r1.claim: The commentators explain that the whole earth became constricted and their own selves felt tight from anxiety and loneliness.

THALABI:v5p108/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p108/r2.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
THALABI:v5p108/r2.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq defines sincere repentance as the constriction felt by Kaʿb and his companions even though the earth was spacious.

THALABI:v5p108/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v5p108/r3.speaker: أبو يزيد
THALABI:v5p108/r3.claim: Abu Yazid says he mistakenly thought he loved God, pleased Him, remembered Him, and repented, then learned God had first loved, approved, remembered, and accepted him.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r1.speaker: الضحاك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r1.claim: Al-Dahhak and Abu Malik say the three were left behind from repentance, with their acceptance delayed; they had not tied themselves to Abu Lubaba.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r2.speaker: عكرمة
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r2.claim: Ikrima says they were left behind from the Prophet's expedition.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r3.claim: The three were Hilal ibn Umayya, Murara ibn al-Rabi, and Ka'b ibn Malik.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r4.claim: The earth felt constricted because Muslims stopped speaking to them, and their own selves because they endured this estrangement.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r5.claim: They knew that only God could be a refuge who might pardon them and accept their repentance.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r6.speaker: كعب بن مالك
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r6.claim: Ka'b ibn Malik says God accepted their repentance fifty nights after the Prophet returned from the Tabuk expedition.

MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v2p412/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas takes 'so that they might repent' to mean becoming steadfast; their repentance had preceded the test, which was meant to reform them and others.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r1.claim: The three left behind are those deferred in 9:106, and the phrase means that God accepted their repentance; Ibn Abbas and Mujahid say they were held back from its acceptance.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r2.claim: Kaʿb ibn Malik, one of the three who stayed without excuse, says their absence was not the point: the Prophet had postponed deciding their case, as 9:106 says.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r3.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84#2/r3.claim: The earth felt constricted because believers would not speak or trade with the three, their wives were told to separate, and the Prophet turned away until their pardon after fifty days.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84/r2.claim: The repeated mention of God's repentance is not redundant: pardon comes first as grace before the sin is mentioned, then is repeated; it may also mean mercy upon mercy.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84/r3.speaker: رسول الله
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p84/r3.claim: The Prophet says God forgives a Muslim's sin twenty times; Ibn Abbas glosses 'then He turned to them' as increased approval.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r1.claim: The constriction of their selves is distress in their hearts and loneliness when no believer spoke to them; they knew there was no refuge from God's punishment except with Him.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r2.speaker: صاحب النظم
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r2.claim: The order of the verse implies that recognizing their sin included an inward request for repentance; God accepted and showed mercy to that sincere intention before the text resumes with 'then He turned to them'.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r3.claim: The second mention of God's turning to them emphasizes increased approval and protection.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r4.claim: God's turning to them 'so that they might repent' means He gently enabled and guided them; without His will and enabling, a servant cannot repent.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r5.speaker: ابن الأنباري
WAHIDI-BASIT:v11p85/r5.claim: Ibn al-Anbari also reads the phrase as God's turning so they persist in repentance or benefit from its reward; both depend on God's prior turning to them.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r4.claim: The three left behind had their repentance delayed; the author identifies them with the people mentioned in 9:106.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r5.claim: The earth felt constricted because people shunned them, refusing dealings and conversation; their own selves felt constricted through anguish.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r6.claim: They became certain that no refuge from God's punishment existed except with God himself.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:9:117-118/r7.claim: God graciously enabled and guided them to repent.

JISHUMI:v5p3256/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3256/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v5p3256/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the three delayed their decision and did not confess their sins; they were not hardened hypocrites but deferred, to be forgiven if they repented and punished if they persisted.

JISHUMI:v5p3256/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3256/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3256/r2.claim: Another account says they had repented, but God then revealed the verse naming the three and accepted their repentance.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r1.claim: The common passive reading خلفوا means they were left behind by others; ʿIkrima's active form means they stayed back after the Messenger and failed in their duty.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r10.claim: Exegetes agree the verse concerns Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ, and Hilāl ibn Umayya, believers who stayed behind with hypocrites and offered excuses; they numbered among more than eighty who stayed.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r11.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r11.claim: Al-Aṣamm says the three were Muslims without hypocrisy: one stayed to tend his land, one was newly married, and the third had neither family nor property and was negligent.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r2.speaker: عكرمة
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r2.claim: ʿIkrima reads خلفوا with both consonants open and no doubling, deriving it from staying behind after the Messenger.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r3.speaker: جعفر بن محمد الصادق
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r3.claim: Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq reads خالفوا, meaning they opposed or acted differently.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r5.claim: Khalf can mean the opposite of front, a successor, or poor speech; the lexicon also explains خلفه and related forms for substitution and succession.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r6.claim: Raḥb means breadth or spaciousness, as in welcoming someone with room, describing a wide place, or urging horses to spread out.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r7.claim: A maljaʾ is a place of refuge; to take refuge is to seek protection there, while iljāʾ means compelling someone into a place by preventing alternatives.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r8.claim: The conjunction in وعلى الثلاثة coordinates them with God's repentance toward the Prophet and Emigrants; الثلاثة identifies a known trio, not a generic three.

JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v5p3284#2/r9.claim: لا ملجأ is accusative under negation, as in لا رفث; it may also be written with nunation to mean that there is no refuge.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p105/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p105/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p105/r5.claim: The three had stayed behind from Tabuk; alternatively, their case was deferred after Abu Lubaba and his companions repented. They were Kaab ibn Malik, Marara ibn al-Rabi, and Hilal ibn Umayya, all Ansar.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p105/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p105/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p105/r6.claim: Kaab ibn Malik’s account says he had never missed an expedition with the Prophet except Tabuk and, earlier, Badr, whose absentees were not reproached.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r1.claim: Kaab recounts the Prophet’s joyful welcome and promise that this was Kaab’s best day since birth, confirmed as good news from God.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r2.claim: Kaab offered all his wealth as charity in repentance, but the Prophet told him to keep some; Kaab retained his share at Khaybar.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r3.claim: Kaab vowed to tell only the truth for the rest of his life, crediting his salvation to truthful speech; the revelation then commanded believers to be with the truthful.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r4.speaker: إسحاق بن راشد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r4.claim: Ishaq ibn Rashid transmits from al-Zuhri, via Kaab, that the Prophet forbade people to speak to the three, leaving Kaab fearing he might die without the Prophet praying over him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r5.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p108/r5.claim: In Ishaq’s report, God revealed their repentance in the night at Umm Salama’s; she wanted to announce it, but the Prophet waited until after dawn prayer so crowds would not keep them awake.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r1.claim: The earth’s apparent breadth narrowed for them, and their own selves narrowed with grief and anxiety.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r2.claim: Their conviction that there was no refuge from God means certainty that there is no escape from Him except by returning to Him.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v4p109/r3.claim: God’s renewed repentance means they should remain steadfast in repentance, which had already begun before this verse.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r1.claim: The three are Kaʿb ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabiʿ, and Hilal ibn Umayya.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r10.speaker: أبو خيثمة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r10.claim: Abu Khaythama left his shaded garden, fresh dates, cold water, and beautiful wife to catch the Prophet; the Prophet recognized the approaching rider and rejoiced.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r2.claim: They were left behind from the expedition; alternatively, they lagged behind Abu Lubaba and his companions, whose repentance had been accepted earlier.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r3.claim: Readings include ‘they were left behind’ or ‘they left the warriors in Medina’; Jaʿfar al-Sadiq read خالفوا, and al-Aʿmash read المخلفين.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r4.claim: The earth being spacious yet constricted is a metaphor for their bewilderment and agitation, unable to settle anywhere.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r5.claim: Their selves means their hearts, which could hold no comfort or joy because of their loneliness and grief.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r6.claim: ‘They thought’ means they knew there was no refuge from God's anger except turning to Him for forgiveness.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r7.claim: God repeatedly accepted them with mercy so they would persist in repentance and repent again after future slips, since He accepts repeated repentance.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r8.speaker: الحسن
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r8.claim: Hasan recounts three believers who gave up a valuable orchard, attachment to family, or love of life and joined the Prophet; he concludes believers repent without persisting in sin.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r9.speaker: أبو ذر الغفاري
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p303/r9.claim: Abu Dharr's camel lagged, so he carried his belongings and followed the Prophet on foot; the Prophet prayed that Abu Dharr walk, die, and be raised alone, with mercy.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r1.claim: The three remained behind and did not catch up with the Prophet.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r2.speaker: كعب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r2.claim: Kaʿb recounts the Prophet's stern response on his return, the community's silence, separation from wives after forty nights, and the announcement after fifty nights that God had accepted them; he prostrated, was greeted by Talha, and heard the Prophet call it his best day since birth.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r3.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p305/r3.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq defines sincere repentance as feeling the earth and one's own soul constrict, like Kaʿb and his two companions.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r3.speaker: قتادة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r3.claim: Qatada says خُلِّفوا means they were left behind from the Tabuk expedition; Ka'b himself rejects this, explaining that they were left pending acceptance of their excuses, not because they failed to join the campaign.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r4.claim: Ibn Atiyya prefers 'left pending their excuse' because the constriction of the earth marks the endpoint of that decision, not the fact they had stayed behind from the campaign.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r5.speaker: الجمهور
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r5.claim: The majority read خُلِّفوا with ḍamma on خ and a doubled lām; other readers offer several vocalized forms, including المخلفين and خالفوا.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r6.speaker: أبو جعفر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r6.claim: Abu Ja'far says that if the word meant simply 'left behind' in the passive sense, the three would have had no sin.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r7.claim: بما رحبت means 'with its spaciousness,' with ما as a verbal noun; their selves narrowing is a metaphor for grief and distress filling them, and ظنوا means they knew with certainty.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p93#2/r8.claim: Because the passage counts blessings, it first names God's action in turning toward them so that they could repent; when recounting wrongdoing, the order instead begins with the wrongdoer, as in 61:5, to stress culpability.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r1.claim: The episode's full explanation depends on the detailed hadith of the three in the cited books; their sin was grave because the law expects greater diligence from people of standing, who serve as examples and evidence against hypocrites and critics. Ka'b was from al-Aqaba and his companions from Badr.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r2.speaker: الأوزاعي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r2.claim: In a letter to al-Mansur Abu Ja'far, al-Awza'i says kinship to the Prophet increases one's duty to God and obedience, and makes people's censure stronger when one acts against it; al-Tanukhi's verse likewise says a great person's fault is great.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p94/r3.claim: One route says the Prophet was at Umm Salama's home on the night their repentance was revealed; when she offered to summon them, he said the crowds would keep them awake all night.

TABRISI:9:117-118#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#2/r2.claim: Khullifū means they were left behind and stayed; khālafū means they opposed and therefore stayed back.

TABRISI:9:117-118#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#2/r4.claim: The earth narrowing despite its breadth describes extreme remorse; ẓann here means certainty, as in Duraid b. al-Ṣimma's poem.

TABRISI:9:117-118#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#3/r1.claim: The three are Kaʿb b. Mālik, Murāra b. al-Rabīʿ, and Hilāl b. Umayya, who stayed back from the expedition through laxity rather than hypocrisy, regretted it, and were shunned for fifty days until God accepted their repentance.

TABRISI:9:117-118#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#3/r9.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:9:117-118#3/r9.claim: Mujāhid says the three were left behind from acceptance of repentance after other people, including hypocrites, had been pardoned, like the group deferred to God's decision in 9:106.

TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r1.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r1.claim: Al-Ḥasan and Qatāda say the three were left behind from the Tabūk campaign; the Ahl al-Bayt reading “opposed” means they acted contrary to the Prophet, and if they had merely been left behind they would not merit blame.

TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r2.claim: Their world became constricted despite its breadth, describing the furthest degree of remorse; the Prophet had ordered people not to speak or sit with them while their repentance was delayed.

TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#4/r3.claim: Their ostracism was not a rejection of repentance: they were still commanded to repent, and God delayed revealing acceptance to intensify the trial and reform them and others against repeating the offense.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r1.claim: The constriction of their souls is hyperbole for such grief that they seemed to have nowhere to hide themselves.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r10.claim: Another coherence reading says that after declaring His sovereignty and that none can help apart from Him, God immediately demonstrates mercy by accepting believers' repentance.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r2.claim: An alternative explains their constriction as the tightness of their breasts from the worry within them.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r3.claim: They became certain that no refuge could protect them from God except God, and that repentance alone could save them from His punishment.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r4.claim: God made repentance easy for them, and they then repented.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r5.claim: An alternative reads their repentance as a return to their former condition before the sin.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r6.claim: Another reading says God accepted the three men's repentance and disclosed it to the Prophet so believers would repent, knowing God accepts repentance.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r7.speaker: الحسن
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r7.claim: Hasan says they shed no blood, took no property, and severed no kinship; they lagged behind the Prophet's expedition for property, family, or rest, then regretted it and repented.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r8.claim: Al-Tawwab means the One who accepts repentance repeatedly, and al-Rahim describes His compassion toward His servants.

TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r9.speaker: أبو مسلم
TABRISI:9:117-118#5/r9.claim: Abu Muslim links the verse to the earlier praise of those who repent: God now shows acceptance of their repentance and approval for following the Prophet in hardship.

TABRISI:9:117-118/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118/r2.speaker: علي بن الحسين
TABRISI:9:117-118/r2.claim: The common reading says the three were left behind; ʿAlī b. al-Ḥusayn, Abū Jaʿfar, and Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq read “they differed/opposed.”

TABRISI:9:117-118/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:9:117-118/r3.speaker: عكرمة
TABRISI:9:117-118/r3.claim: ʿIkrima, Zirr b. Ḥubaysh, and ʿAmr b. ʿUbayd read the verb with a light consonant and fatḥa on khāʾ and lām, meaning left in the rear.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r1.speaker: أبو رزين وأبو مجلز والشعبي وابن يعمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r1.claim: They read khalafu with an alif; other named readers have variants with a light or geminated lām.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r2.claim: These are the people called “others deferred” in 9:106; their names were given earlier.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r3.claim: Kullifu means left behind from repentance: these people did not submit as Abu Lubaba and his companions had.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r4.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p512#2/r4.claim: Kullifu means left behind from the Tabuk expedition; their story belongs with Ka'b ibn Malik's repentance.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r1.claim: The earth felt narrow despite its breadth because Muslims were ordered to avoid business and conversation with the three, isolate them from their wives, and the Prophet turned away from them.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r2.claim: Their own selves felt constricted by grief and anxiety; zannu means they became certain there was no refuge from God or His punishment except in Him.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r3.claim: God's renewed turning to them emphasizes repentance; “so that they repent” means enabling them to be steadfast or to continue repentance without undoing it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r4.claim: Another explanation says God enabled them to persist in repentance and not return to what would undo it.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v3p513/r5.claim: Sincere repentance was described as constricting the earth and the penitent's own soul, like Ka'b and his two companions experienced.

RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r1.claim: The three are conjoined to the Prophet, emigrants, and Helpers whose repentance was accepted; being named alongside the Prophet raises their standing and places their acceptance in the same account.

RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r2.claim: The three are those deferred in 9:106; خلفوا need not mean their staying was ordered or approved, but can simply state that they remained behind, perhaps despite a prohibition.

RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r3.claim: A second explanation is that the three intended to go to battle but received time to gather equipment; when they delayed through laxity, the Prophet left them behind.

RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r4.claim: A third explanation takes خلفوا to mean that their repentance was deferred after the first group; Ka'b ibn Malik says it refers to the Messenger delaying his judgment, as with those deferred to God's command in 9:106.

RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p172#2/r5.claim: The source notes variants: خلفوا can mean they were left in Medina behind the fighters and derives from successor or stale-mouth terms; Ja'far al-Sadiq reads خالفوا, and al-A'mash reads المخلفين.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r1.speaker: المفسرون
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r1.claim: The constriction of the earth refers to the Prophet turning away, forbidding believers to speak to the three, and ordering their wives to separate from them for fifty days or more.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r10.claim: A final reading is that God accepted them so they could benefit from repentance and receive its reward; those benefits follow God's acceptance.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r2.claim: Their souls were constricted by grief, loneliness from loved ones, and the contemptuous way people looked at them.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r3.claim: Some interpret ظنوا as they knew there was no refuge from God except in Him; the verse praises them, and this meaning is supported by the same verb in 2:46.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r4.claim: Others say they awaited revelation without certainty that God would clear them of hypocrisy, while allowing that their hardship might last longer.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r5.claim: An implied first statement that God accepted them makes the repetition of ثم تاب عليهم emphatic, like a ruler repeating that he pardons a servant.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r6.speaker: أصحابنا
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r6.claim: The Ashʿarite reading distinguishes God's creating repentance from the servants' act of repenting, as in verses that attribute laughter, weeping, and movement to both God and people.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r7.claim: Another interpretation is that God's earlier acceptance was meant to prompt their later repentance.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r8.claim: Because repentance means returning, the phrase can mean God restored them to fellowship with believers and ended their isolation.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173#2/r9.claim: It can also mean that God's acceptance enabled them to persist in repentance rather than undo it.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r1.claim: The three left behind were Kaʿb b. Mālik, Hilāl b. Umayya, and Murāra b. al-Rabīʿ.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r2.claim: One account says the three followed the Prophet after renouncing the property, family, or attachment to life that had delayed them; revelation then described them among those deferred.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r3.speaker: كعب
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r3.claim: The majority account says they did not pursue the Prophet: Kaʿb confessed that his mount and provisions were ready, but his sin had held him back, and the Prophet declined to ask God to forgive him.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r4.speaker: كعب
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r4.claim: The three were socially shunned for fifty days or longer; after Hilāl's wife reported his weeping, the revelation arrived and the Prophet announced their acceptance.

RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r5.speaker: كعب
RAZI-FULL:v16p173/r5.claim: After his repentance was accepted, Kaʿb offered all his wealth as charity, then half; the Prophet refused both and accepted a third.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r1.claim: Ka‘b says he had never missed a campaign except Tabuk and Badr; no one was reproached for Badr because the Muslims had set out for the Quraysh caravan and unexpectedly met their enemy.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r2.claim: Ka‘b says the pledge at al-‘Aqaba mattered more to him than participation at Badr, despite Badr’s greater public fame.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r3.claim: Ka‘b had never been stronger or wealthier than before Tabuk and gathered two mounts, while the expedition meant extreme heat, long travel, desert, and a large enemy.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r4.claim: The Prophet announced the destination openly so Muslims could prepare; their large numbers were not recorded in a register, making a would-be absentee think revelation might not expose him.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r5.claim: Ripe fruit and shade drew Ka‘b’s attention; he kept postponing preparations, assuming he could catch up, until the army had gone too far.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r6.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r6.claim: After the departure, Ka‘b felt isolated because he saw only a suspected hypocrite or someone excused by God among those left in Medina.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r7.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r7.claim: At Tabuk the Prophet asked about Ka‘b; one man blamed his clothes and vanity, but Mu‘adh ibn Jabal defended him as a man known for good, and the Prophet kept silent.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r8.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#2/r8.claim: The Prophet recognized the approaching figure as Abu Khaythama, who had donated a measure of dates and been mocked by hypocrites.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r1.claim: As the Prophet returned, Ka‘b considered a lie but chose truth; on arrival the Prophet prayed two units in the mosque and received over eighty absentees, accepting their oaths outwardly and leaving their inner truth to God.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r2.claim: Ka‘b confessed to the Prophet that he had no excuse and had been able and wealthy enough to go; he said a false excuse might satisfy the Prophet but anger God.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r3.claim: The Prophet said Ka‘b had spoken truthfully and ordered him to wait until God decided his case.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r4.claim: Men from Banu Salama urged Ka‘b to invent an excuse, and he nearly returned to retract his truth; hearing Murara and Hilal had done likewise steadied him.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#3/r5.claim: The Prophet singled out the three for a ban on speaking; after fifty nights of estrangement, Ka‘b continued prayer and market visits while the others stayed home weeping.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r1.claim: Ka‘b sought reassurance from his cousin Abu Qatada, but after repeated questions about his love for God and the Messenger, Abu Qatada answered only that God and His Messenger know.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r2.claim: A Syrian merchant delivered a letter from the king of Ghassan offering Ka‘b refuge; Ka‘b regarded it as another trial and burned it.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r3.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r3.claim: After forty of the fifty nights, the Prophet ordered the three to separate from their wives without divorcing them; Hilal’s wife could serve him but not have marital relations.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r4.claim: Ka‘b declined to request the same service permission given to Hilal’s wife, unsure what the Prophet would say to a young man.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r5.claim: On the fiftieth morning, while he sat under the constriction described in the verse, a herald on Mount Sala announced good news and Ka‘b prostrated, recognizing relief.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r6.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r6.claim: The Prophet announced God’s acceptance after the dawn prayer; people congratulated Ka‘b, and Talha ibn Ubayd Allah ran to greet him, the only Muhajir to do so.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r7.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r7.claim: The Prophet told Ka‘b that this was the best day since his birth and confirmed that the good news came from God.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r8.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r8.claim: Ka‘b offered all his property as charity for repentance, but the Prophet advised him to keep some; Ka‘b kept his share at Khaybar and pledged to speak only truth.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r9.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#4/r9.claim: Ka‘b greeted the Prophet after prayer but received no answer and saw him turn away whenever Ka‘b looked toward him.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r1.claim: Ka‘b says the revealed passage included God’s repentance for the Prophet and believers, the three left behind, and the command to fear God and stay with the truthful.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r2.claim: After Islam, Ka‘b considered truthful speech his greatest blessing; lying would have destroyed him like the liars, whom God censured severely.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r3.claim: Ka‘b again explains that the three were deferred from the accepted excuse-makers, so ‘left behind’ means their case was postponed rather than that they failed to campaign.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r4.claim: ‘The earth narrowed despite its breadth’ means that the three were socially shunned, neither dealt with nor spoken to; the passage supports shunning sinners until they repent.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r5.claim: Their own selves narrowed through grief and loneliness caused by the companions’ coldness.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r6.claim: They became certain that only God could grant them pardon and accept their repentance.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r7.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#5/r7.claim: Abu Bakr al-Warraq defines sincere repentance by the distress of the earth and self, as in Ka‘b and his two companions.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r1.claim: God began the process by accepting their repentance, enabling them to repent; divine acceptance precedes the human act of repentance.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r2.speaker: أبو زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r2.claim: Abu Zayd describes four reversals: he thought he first loved God, pleased Him, remembered Him, and repented, but God had first loved, approved, remembered, and accepted him.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r3.claim: An alternative reads ‘so that they might repent’ as ‘so that they remain steadfast in repentance,’ as in the command for believers to believe.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118#6/r4.claim: Another interpretation says God gave them respite and did not hasten punishment, unlike the punishment imposed on the Jews.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r1.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r1.claim: Mujahid and Abu Malik say the three were left behind from repentance.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r2.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r2.claim: Qatada says they were left behind from the Tabuk campaign.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r3.speaker: محمد بن زيد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r3.claim: Muhammad ibn Zayd explains the phrase as their being left behind, since leaving someone means separating while he remains seated.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r4.speaker: عكرمة بن خالد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r4.claim: Ikrima ibn Khalid reads the word to mean they remained in the Prophet’s wake.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r5.speaker: جعفر بن محمد
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r5.claim: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad is reported to have read the word as ‘they dissented.’

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r6.claim: The preferred explanation is that the three were deferred and their case postponed: unlike hypocrites or excused absentees, the Prophet delayed judgment until revelation, as the sound reports establish.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r7.speaker: كعب بن مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r7.claim: Ka‘b clarifies that ‘left behind’ refers to the Prophet postponing their case after accepting the others’ excuses, not their failure to join the campaign.

QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:9:118/r8.claim: The three were Ka‘b ibn Malik, Murara ibn al-Rabi‘ al-‘Amiri, and Hilal ibn Umayya al-Waqifi, all from the Ansar.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r1.claim: The three whose repentance was accepted were Ka'b ibn Malik, Hilal ibn Umayya, and Murara ibn al-Rabi.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r2.claim: Khullifu may mean they stayed behind from the expedition or that their case was deferred.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r3.claim: The earth's vastness felt constricting because everyone turned away from them; the heart's constriction means such grief that it could hold neither comfort nor joy.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r4.claim: They knew there was no refuge from God's displeasure except in seeking Him; God enabled them to repent and either accepted them so they could remain repentant or repeatedly accepted them to keep them steadfast.

BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:9:118/r5.claim: God is repeatedly accepting of repentance, even if someone returns to sin many times daily, and mercifully favors them with blessings.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r1.claim: The three left behind from the campaign were Kaʿb ibn Mālik, Murāra ibn al-Rabīʿ, and Hilāl ibn Umayya.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r2.claim: The earth's constriction despite its breadth depicts their confusion and agitation; their hearts could hold neither comfort nor joy, and they knew no refuge from God's anger except seeking forgiveness.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r3.claim: God accepted their repentance after fifty days so that they could join the repentant.

NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r4.speaker: أبو بكر الوراق
NASAFI-FULL:v2p113/r4.claim: Al-Warrāq defines sincere repentance as making earth and one's own soul feel constricted, as happened to these three.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r2.speaker: قتادة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r2.claim: Qatāda says the three were left behind from the Tabūk expedition.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r3.claim: Another view says they were left pending after Abū Lubāba’s group was forgiven; their case was delayed fifty days before their repentance was accepted.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r4.claim: Kaʿb ibn Mālik himself rejected the physical-delay interpretation: they were left without acceptance of their excuses, not simply left behind on the expedition.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r5.claim: Readers vary between passive ‘they were left behind’ forms, active ‘they left behind the fighters’ or ‘became corrupt,’ and ‘they differed’ with an added alif; al-Bāqir says the passive gloss would not fit.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r6.claim: Al-Aʿmash’s ‘the three left behind’ is likely an explanatory reading because it differs from the consonantal codex text.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r7.claim: The constriction of the earth is a figure for isolation; the constriction of their selves depicts grief and anxiety filling them so fully that no comfort or joy could enter.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r8.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r8.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads ‘they thought’ as ‘they knew’; Ibn ʿAṭiyya glosses it as certainty, while another view keeps ordinary conjecture because the duration of their hardship remained uncertain.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p519/r9.claim: The verse’s sequence moves from social alienation, to inward distress, and finally to despair of human help and complete turning to God alone.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects treating thumma as extra or making the clause after it the conditional answer, since Arabic usage does not support an extra thumma.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r2.claim: Others take ‘when’ after ‘until’ as a temporal endpoint without conditional force: they were left until that time, then God again accepted them and showed mercy.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r3.claim: ‘So that they repent’ can mean staying firm in repentance and not undoing it, or returning to their usual social intercourse with believers and regaining calm.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r4.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya says the verse begins with God’s action when recounting a divine favor, but begins with the sinner when describing blame, as in 16:100.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r5.claim: The full account of the three is in al-Bukhārī and Muslim’s expedition reports, so the commentator abbreviates it.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r6.claim: Their offense merited severity because leaders and exemplars bear greater responsibility; Kaʿb was an ʿAqaba veteran and his companions were veterans of Badr, unlike ordinary men.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r7.speaker: الأوزاعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v5p520/r7.claim: Al-Awzāʿī’s letter to Caliph al-Manṣūr says kinship with the Prophet only increases one’s duty to God and the public’s right to object when one disobeys.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r1.claim: أن is the lightened form that supplies both objects; لا and its phrase form the predicate, with من الله as the predicate of لا.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r2.claim: لا may not govern ملجأ here with إلا إليه as its predicate, since the long noun would need inflection.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r3.speaker: بعضهم
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r3.claim: Some allow a long indefinite noun to imitate a construct and lose its nunation, citing poetry and لا صمت يوم إلى الليل.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:118#2/r4.claim: إلا إليه excludes from an omitted general phrase: there is no refuge to anyone except to God, like لا إله إلا الله.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r1.claim: وعلى الثلاثة can coordinate with النبي or with the pronoun in عليهم; the repeated preposition supports the latter parse.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r2.claim: The majority read خُلِّفوا passively with a doubled lam; Abu Malik also reads it passively but with a light lam.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r3.speaker: عكرمة وزر بن حبيش وعمر بن عبيد وعكرمة بن هارون المخزومي ومعاذ القارئ
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r3.claim: These readers use the active, light-lam form: the men were left behind or were morally corrupt, like the stale breath of a fasting person.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r4.speaker: أبو العالية وأبو الجوزاء
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r4.claim: Abu al-Aliya and Abu al-Jawza read the active form with a doubled lam.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r5.speaker: أبو رزين وعلي بن الحسين وزيد ومحمد الباقر وجعفر الصادق
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r5.claim: They read خالفوا with an alif, meaning the three did not join the expedition or agree with those who went out.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r6.speaker: الباقر
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r6.claim: Al-Baqir comments, ولو خلفوا لم يكن لهم, distinguishing the خالفوا reading from خلفوا.

SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:9:118/r7.claim: Here ظن may mean knowledge, as in the cited line addressed to a group told to expect two thousand armed men, or it may retain its ordinary sense.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r1.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r1.claim: Kaʿb says he missed no expedition except Tabuk, apart from Badr, where absentees were not blamed; he valued the Aqaba pledge more than Badr despite Badr's greater fame.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r2.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r2.claim: Badr had been an unintended meeting: the Messenger set out for Quraysh's caravan, and God brought the two sides together without an appointment.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r3.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r3.claim: Kaʿb was more able and prosperous than ever, having assembled two mounts for Tabuk, but the campaign came in severe heat across a distant, difficult route against many enemies.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r4.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r4.claim: The Prophet usually concealed a campaign's destination, but disclosed Tabuk so Muslims could prepare for its distant journey and numerous enemy; the large force had no roster.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r5.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r5.claim: Though fruit and shade made the expedition appealing, Kaʿb repeatedly postponed preparations, expecting to catch up, until the army departed and he could not complete his equipment.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r6.speaker: كعب بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p229/r6.claim: After the army left, Kaʿb regretted not pursuing it; among those remaining he saw only a suspected hypocrite or someone excused by God, and the Prophet did not ask about him until Tabuk.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p230/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v4p230/r1.speaker: رجل من بني سلمة
